provider: U.S. Department of Defense

financialStatusHistory.note: DoD announced the award on 16 April 2024. The release does not date the award decision, and the agreement's signing date (11 April 2024, below) precedes the announcement, so the announcement date is not used as the decision date.

USAspending records cooperative agreement FA86502425501 to 5N PLUS SEMICONDUCTORS LLC as a new award signed 11 April 2024, described as DPA Title III sustainment and enhancement of the space-qualified solar cell supply chain (the subject of DoD's release). That federal award record establishes an executed agreement; the agreement text was not inspected. A later modification dated 20 May 2025 is described as definitizing the agreement. Binding describes the agreement, not paid money. Amounts, kept distinct: the federal obligation reported in the record is $12,458,128 (award plus modifications through 26 March 2026) and its non-federal funding is $2,505,981; neither equals the $14.4M announced figure, which is kept as stated, and how the announced figure relates to them is not reconciled.

Federal-reporting attribution only: neither DoD nor 5N+ states a payment, receivable or payment date. USAspending's File C (account-by-award) data, reported by DoD on federal account 097-0360 and linked to this award by its FAIN, carry three gross-outlay lines, each a fiscal-year-beginning-to-period-end figure: $998,701.28 (FY2024 period 9, ending June 2024), $1,032,342.24 (FY2025 period 9, ending June 2025) and $399,308.73 (FY2026 period 6, ending March 2026). By the official definition (OMB Circular A-11, quoted in USAspending's data dictionary) an outlay is a payment made to liquidate an obligation, so some money is reported paid out against this agreement. A reporting period is not a payment date, so the date is left null. The lines name no payee, each is only a floor for its fiscal year at that period end, and they are not totalled, so no amount paid is recorded. The award summary's $0 account outlay does not contradict them: USAspending counts toward that field only each fiscal year's latest closed DoD submission, and the same $0 appears on other awards on this account that carry interim outlay lines. Year-end data differ by year: for FY2024 the period-12 submission is available and holds account rows for other awards but no outlay line for this award; for FY2025 the period-12 submission is available but the File C data retrieved hold no rows for the account in it; for FY2026 no year-end submission existed at retrieval on 4 October 2026 (the latest DoD submission was period 11), so that year's position is open. The public data do not show whether the award was omitted or reported as zero, and omission is the usual pattern (10 of 13 FY2024 assistance awards with a period-9 outlay line have none at period 12). This is the corpus's first partial disbursement resting on federal-reporting data and not on a government or recipient statement. The entry is undated and reflects evidence reviewed on 4 October 2026; it does not establish that any disbursement had occurred at an earlier date, although derivations that read the latest entry show it at every as-of date. The reading is left to human review.
